headline: Rebuilt from raw microdata and validated against the replication, CDLZ's minimum-wage findings HELD but SOFTENED through the $15-era: no window shows significant job loss, yet the central employment estimate drifted from +2.8% (1979-2016) to about zero/slightly negative pooled through 2024.

tables.title: How the findings evolved, by event-cohort (QCEW-benchmarked bunching event study)

figures.caption: Evolution of the three CDLZ findings across five event-cohorts, 1979-2024, vs the paper's pooled reference bands. A: net affected employment (%Demp); B: affected wage gain; C: the bunching signature (missing jobs below new MW approx equal excess jobs above) in every era.
figures.alt: Three stacked panels over calendar year 1980-2025. Top: percent change in affected employment per cohort with 95% CIs, hovering around a dashed +2.8% CDLZ line, dipping to -4% for the 2016-2019 cohort. Middle: affected wage gains, all positive near the +6.8% line. Bottom: excess (blue) and missing (orange) jobs, mirror images across all cohorts.

figures.caption: Figure II analog: employment change by wage bin relative to the new minimum, original 1979-2016 events (blue) vs new $15-era 2016-2024 events (orange). Both show missing jobs just below (k=-1) and excess at/just above (k=0..2) the new MW; the new era spreads the excess more broadly (larger spillover).
figures.alt: Line plot of employment change per dollar bin from k=-4 to +4. Both series dip sharply negative at k=-1 and spike positive at k=0-2, then flatten; near-identical missing-jobs trough, new-era excess more spread out.

notes: Pipeline rebuilt from raw NBER MORG + Census CPS and validated against the replication's shipped panel: treatment dummies match exactly, 138 prominent events reproduced exactly, anchor regression reproduces the paper (Da=0.021, Db=-0.018, E=0.571).
QCEW benchmarking APPLIED (spec marked optional) via BLS open API, validated corr=1.00 vs the shipped 2016 file; it materially affects the employment normalization.
2025 from Census monthly CPS (MORG ends 2024); Oct 2025 CPS/CPI missing (govt shutdown) so 2025q4 uses Nov+Dec. CPI-U-RS spliced with CPI-U growth after 2016.

No window or Kaitz-half shows STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT job loss; the shift is in the central estimate, concentrated in high-bite 2016-2019 and Kaitz>=0.5 events, hinting the disemployment frontier lies near the top of the newly observed Kaitz range (~0.6-0.67).
